run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T09:02:32Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on frontend-proxy is explained by a burst of HTTP 504 upstream-response-timeout responses on the /api/recommendations path. frontend-proxy error spans (only on span_name "ingress") went from 0-0.007/s before 09:00 to 0.096-0.159/s between 09:05 and 09:09, and 62.65 ERROR ingress spans were counted against 19,072.77 non-error ingress spans in 08:42-09:12 (span counts, not unique requests). Its own access log shows "GET /api/recommendations?productIds=... 504 UT response_timeout" with 14999-15001 ms durations at 09:04-09:07, and a full trace shows the frontend taking 22.08 s (200) because its child gRPC call to RecommendationService/ListRecommendations took 22.079 s while the proxy abandoned the request at 15 s. Independently, container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods_total/container_cpu_cfs_periods_total for container recommendation of pod recommendation-5f45f75855-htttv rose from 3.5-7% (08:38-08:59) to 32.6% at 09:00, 85.5% at 09:01 and 95-97% from 09:02 through 09:11, making it the most throttled pod in otel-demo (next highest 24.7%) while frontend throttling was unchanged from its pre-incident level. Chaos-mesh events record nine StressChaos experiments named otel-demo-recommendation-cpu-stress-* being applied for ~55 s each to otel-demo/recommendation-5f45f75855-htttv/recommendation between 08:59:28 and 09:07:28. Frontend-proxy, frontend, product-catalog and traffic volume were checked and do not explain the failure. The causal link from the injected CPU stress to the recommendation latency/telemetry stall is stated as a hypothesis, and why throttling stayed at 95%+ after the last observed chaos event, and after 09:08, is unresolved.

claims.text: frontend-proxy STATUS_CODE_ERROR span rate on span_name "ingress" was 0-0.0074/s from 08:39 to 08:59, then 0.0259/s at 09:03, 0.0963/s at 09:05, 0.148/s at 09:07, 0.159/s at 09:09 and 0.0667/s at 09:11; the corresponding non-error (UNSET) ingress rate stayed in 6.6-13.0/s throughout, i.e. no traffic surge.
In 08:42-09:12 frontend-proxy ingress counted 62.65 spans with status_code STATUS_CODE_ERROR against 19072.77 spans with STATUS_CODE_UNSET (span counts, not requests; relative error share ~0.33%).
The 2-minute increase of frontend-proxy error spans was 0-2.7 per window before 09:01 and peaked at 38.7 in the window ending at the 09:06 point, i.e. the error surge began at about 09:01-09:02.

frontend-proxy access-log records show "GET /api/recommendations?productIds=... HTTP/1.1" 504 UT response_timeout with upstream durations 14999-15001 ms; the 20 newest of 50 matching 504 lines (records 09:04:06-09:07:56) are all /api/recommendations requests.

Trace 1b22375ef202bc584afc76532e269fd9 shows frontend-proxy ingress span 15000638 us with error=true, http.status_code 504, otel.status_code ERROR and its child "router frontend egress" span 15000405 us with http.status_code "0", plus a load-generator GET child span 15002017 us with 504.

In the same trace, service frontend's GET /api/recommendations completed with http.status_code 200 after 22082135 us and its child grpc.oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations took 22079095 us, while the trace contains no span from service recommendation.

Sampled failing traces from 09:06-09:08 show the same pattern repeatedly: the frontend's grpc RecommendationService/ListRecommendations client spans ran 17.8-22.1 s (status 0) and the frontend /api/recommendations spans 19.1-22.1 s with http.status_code 200, i.e. responses completed only after frontend-proxy's 15 s timeout.

CPU throttling of container "recommendation" in pod recommendation-5f45f75855-htttv (throttled CFS periods / CFS periods) was 0.035-0.069 from 08:38 to 08:59, then 0.326 at the 09:00 point, 0.855 at 09:01 and 0.953-0.974 from 09:02 through the last point at 09:11.

At 09:10 pod recommendation-5f45f75855-htttv was the most CPU-throttled pod in namespace otel-demo at 0.964, far above the next pods cart-755465879b-hjqf6 (0.247), postgresql-c7fd45b87-9x9wg (0.237) and frontend-675fd7b5c5-x7pxv (0.222).

Chaos-mesh events show nine StressChaos experiments (otel-demo-recommendation-cpu-stress-jn58v, -gwd9j, -tq59h, -lwlmp, -h7zr7, -6p484, -vmtj8, -flf8h, -q55wg) with Started/Applied messages "Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/recommendation-5f45f75855-htttv/recommendation" at 08:59:28, 09:00:28, 09:01:28, 09:02:28, 09:03:28, 09:04:28, 09:05:28, 09:06:28 and 09:07:28, each followed about 55 s later by "Time up according to the duration" and "Successfully recover chaos".

Recommendation-server latency distribution: 92.5-100% of /oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations spans were <=100 ms at every point from 08:38 to 08:59, falling to 87.2% at the 09:01 point and 64% at the 09:02 point, after which no recommendation duration series has samples.

Client-side latency of the recommendation call degraded in the same window: the share of frontend grpc.oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations spans <=1000 ms was 1.0 (or 0.99) from 08:38 to 09:00, 0.724 at 09:01, 0.206 at 09:02 and 0.043-0.152 from 09:03 to 09:12.

Recommendation span metrics stopped counting spans after the 09:02 point: the 2-minute increase of /oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations, /oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/ListProducts and get_product_list was 33.3 at 09:02 and 0 at every point from 09:03 to 09:12.

The recommendation container runs with limits cpu 100m / memory 160Mi and requests cpu 30m / memory 80Mi (image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-recommendation, 1/1 ready), and pod recommendation-5f45f75855-htttv is Running, ready and has 0 restarts.

The recurring ~55 s CPU-stress experiments on the recommendation container, combined with its 100m CPU limit, starved the recommendation process: its server spans grew from <=100 ms to hundreds of milliseconds to ~1 s, the client-observed call grew to 5-22 s, its span export stopped after ~09:02, and frontend requests exceeded frontend-proxy's 15 s upstream timeout, producing the 504 UT response_timeout errors counted by the alert.

Recommendation-container throttling remained at 95-97% through the last available point (09:11) although the last observed StressChaos event is at 09:07:28 and recovered at about 09:08:23; either the stress series continued without events being captured, or a request backlog built during the stress kept the container pinned at its 100m limit. This is unresolved.

frontend-proxy is not itself the faulty component: its ingress and egress spans have essentially the same duration (15000638 us vs 15000405 us), the egress span carries http.status_code "0", and the access log records response flag "UT response_timeout" at 14999-15001 ms, i.e. the proxy timed out waiting on its upstream frontend.

product-catalog was fast while the recommendation call was slow: its server spans in the failing traces are 65-191 us (ListProducts 65 us; GetProduct 74-191 us), so product-catalog latency does not explain the recommendation-side delay.

Frontend CPU throttling was not new: pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-x7pxv was throttled 0.265 at 08:50, before the incident, and 0.222 at 09:10, while frontend's own child span accounts for 22.079 s of the 22.082 s /api/recommendations request, so frontend CPU limits are not the change that caused the surge.
Traffic/load surge is rejected as the cause: frontend-proxy ingress span rate stayed at 6.6-13.0 per second across the whole degradation and was not higher at the peak than before it.

The fraud-detection container restart/BackOff story (3 restarts, Warning BackOff events 08:37:56-08:42:20) is rejected as the cause of this alert: those events precede the frontend-proxy error surge and are on a service that does not sit on the failing /api/recommendations call path, whose failures are 504 upstream timeouts against the frontend's recommendation call.

Suspend or delete the chaos-mesh schedule that spawns the otel-demo-recommendation-cpu-stress-* StressChaos experiments against otel-demo/recommendation-5f45f75855-htttv, or exclude the recommendation service from CPU-stress experiments; its 100m CPU limit leaves no headroom, so also consider raising the recommendation container CPU limit/requests.

gaps: The chaos-mesh Schedule and StressChaos custom resources could not be read with the available Kubernetes tool set (kind stresschaos was refused and Schedule is not a listable kind), so the schedule's definition, CPU stressor size, duration setting and parent object name are known only from event messages.
Kubernetes events are available only from 08:42:20 onward (older events expired), so whether CPU-stress experiments ran before the first observed one at 08:59:28 is unknown.

No StressChaos event was returned after 09:07:28/09:07:36 although recommendation-container throttling stayed at 95-97% through the last data point at 09:11; the cause of the continued throttling after the last observed experiment is unresolved.

Recommendation's own telemetry stops after the 09:02 point (no recommendation spans in Jaeger after 08:59:43 and zero increase of its span metrics from 09:03 on), so recommendation-side latency, throughput and any application error for 09:03-09:14 are unknown; the query traces_search for recommendation in 09:08:30-09:14:58 returned no traces.
No 24h baseline for frontend-proxy error rate exists in this Prometheus (series data starts around 08:38), so the pre-incident 'background' error level could only be compared against 08:38-08:59.
list_prometheus_rules filtered by rule_name RequestErrorRate returned no rules, so the alert's exact PromQL expression, threshold and evaluation window were not verified.
The change_history integration is not available, so what created or who triggered the chaos-mesh schedule is unknown.

The recommendation access-log query filtered for err|error|warn|fail|timeout|panic|exception returned no matching lines, and its readable lines end at 09:07:36; absence of application error logs is unknown, not proof.
The frontend-proxy 504 log slice shows the newest 20 of 50 matching lines (all /api/recommendations); the remaining 30 matching lines and any other 504 paths are unknown.
Whether frontend-proxy's 15 s response timeout or request pile-up also affected other routes is unknown; only /api/recommendations 504s were observed in the slices examined.
next_steps: Inspect the chaos-mesh Schedule objects in the chaos-mesh namespace (e.g. kubectl -n chaos-mesh get schedules, then -o yaml) to confirm the schedule named otel-demo-recommendation-cpu-stress, its selector, stressors, duration and whether it is still active after 09:08.
Check whether the schedule is still spawning experiments after 09:08 and whether recommendation-container CPU throttling has returned to its ~4-7% baseline.
Review the recommendation Deployment's cpu limit (100m) and request (30m) against its actual demand, since the limit leaves no headroom under injected CPU load.

Confirm the Alertmanager rule expression behind RequestErrorRate (threshold above 0 with a small denominator) so that low-volume background 504s do not page, and compare the 09:01-09:11 error burst against it.
